EPOL 590 · Lecture 1 · A mix of theory and practice

The course in one sentence

How do you build a sense of your field, and its gaps?

Academic literature is at once mundane and mystical. We start with fundamentals — building, annotating, mapping, writing — then ask how AI can make interpretation more critical, analytic and reflexive.

Approach

Move fast, but think harder

Sketch, then revise

  • Quick sketches of a literature review, with AI and its caveats
  • Build intuitions for reviewing and writing up fast
  • Peer review turns a lonely pursuit into a social one

A critical lens on AI

  • Knowledge has always been technical: paper, press, media, the internet
  • Ask how outputs were made and whose knowledge they privilege
  • Technology should make us work harder, not easier

What makes a good research question?

Where questions come from

Literature · which key problems are unsolved?

Events · what is happening, and how do we explain it?

Circumstance · it annoys me that no one can answer this

Disposition · I just love working on X

Sociality · all the cool kids work on X. Should I, or shouldn’t I?

Partly a matter of feel: experienced researchers know one when they see it

Question and literature

Each one steers the other

Not a question from thin air, nor one that waits for a systematic review.

1 · Draft a topic or question

2 · Search it: is it answered?

3 · Refine what remains, and repeat

Practicalities

Does it need an answer, and can you give one?

So what?

Is the answer necessary, or does it provoke a shrug?

Doable?

Or would it take 100 years, a billion dollars, a vast team?

Within reach?

Methods you know, data you can actually access.

Novelty

Has it been answered before?

  • Often not obvious: many literatures and disciplines work on related problems
  • Is it novel for good reasons, or because no one needs it, or research can’t answer it?
  • Will it stay novel while you work?

“No one has studied the impact of [next year’s model] on student learning” — true until it’s released.

Test it against sources, practicalities and novelty

Write it down in the class workspace
